scene-u01-pnew1-3.text: Week 15 · KP06 The DB index and information criteria

scene-u01-pnew1-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew1-5.text: DB index: each cluster finds its most similar neighbor, then the similarities are averaged

scene-u01-pnew1-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew1-6.text: How to read: three clusters of two points each, dashed circles have radius equal to the spread $s_i$, crosses are representatives; arrows below show distances $d_{ij}$ and similarities $R_{ij}$.

scene-u01-pnew1-42.name: text#42
scene-u01-pnew1-42.text: Larger spreads and closer distances mean more similar clusters; smaller DB is better

scene-u01-pnew1-52.name: text#52
scene-u01-pnew1-52.text: $C_1$ and $C_2$ are most alike and pull each other to $0.5$

scene-u01-pnew1-53.name: text#53
scene-u01-pnew1-53.text: Note: $R_i$ takes the maximum; averaging comes last

scene-u01-pnew2-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew2-3.text: Week 15 · KP06 The DB index and information criteria

scene-u01-pnew2-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew2-5.text: $DB_m$ has no monotone trend: the three-group data reach the minimum at $m=3$

scene-u01-pnew2-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew2-6.text: How to read: the left colors the three-group data by the $m=3$ clustering; the right shows $DB_m$ for $k$-means with $m=2,\dots,8$, with the minimum circled.

scene-u01-pnew2-102.name: text#102
scene-u01-pnew2-102.text: Compact, separated clusters: even the most similar neighbor is not very similar

scene-u01-pnew2-130.name: text#130
scene-u01-pnew2-130.text: $m=2$: merged groups have large spread; $m\ge4$: split halves are close

scene-u01-pnew2-133.name: text#133
scene-u01-pnew2-133.text: Misconception: "far-apart clusters always give a small $DB$."

scene-u01-pnew2-134.name: text#134
scene-u01-pnew2-134.text: The numerator of $R_{ij}$ is the sum of spreads: far apart but very loose clusters still give a large $R_{ij}$. DB weighs spread and distance together.

scene-u01-pnew2-136.name: text#136
scene-u01-pnew2-136.text: Three-group data and $DB_m$ computed by code [Added]

scene-u01-pnew3-3.text: Week 15 · KP06 The DB index and information criteria

scene-u01-pnew3-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew3-5.text: Information criteria: fit plus penalty; the heavier the penalty, the fewer clusters chosen

scene-u01-pnew3-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew3-6.text: How to read: the same three-group data ($N=90$) fitted with $m=1,\dots,6$ Gaussians; the dashed gray line is $-2L$, each solid line adds a penalty, and circles mark each minimum.

scene-u01-pnew3-62.name: text#62
scene-u01-pnew3-62.text: $-2L$ keeps shrinking with more clusters; only a penalty makes the curve turn up

scene-u01-pnew3-64.name: text#64
scene-u01-pnew3-64.text: Three penalties $\phi(K)$ and the chosen number of clusters

scene-u01-pnew3-78.name: text#78
scene-u01-pnew3-78.text: Means, covariances, weights (minus one degree of freedom)

scene-u01-pnew3-80.text: EM fits and criterion values computed by code [Added]

steps.label: The Davies–Bouldin index
steps.speakerNotes: R_ij=(s_i+s_j)/d_ij; each cluster keeps its largest R_ij, then average to get DB; the three-cluster hand example gives DB3=0.44.

steps.label: DB against m
steps.speakerNotes: For the three-group data DB_m is smallest at m=3 (0.25); 0.73 at m=2 and 0.65 at m=4; distance alone does not make DB small.

steps.label: Information criteria
steps.speakerNotes: C=-2L+φ(K): -2L keeps falling; AIC picks 6 clusters, Consistent AIC 4, BIC 3; in two dimensions K=6m-1.
